title: Typed comparison of defeasible support before and after an update
independentExamples: A provenance-bearing reliability fact about a nonce device could raise support for a proposition that the device will complete a task.
A newly asserted route obstruction could lower support for a nonce traveler reaching a destination while leaving unrelated propositions unchanged.
preconditions: Premise, hypothesis, and update have been compiled into typed propositions and relations.
Relevant defaults, conflicts, priorities, provenance, and scope are explicit.
The before and after theories have bounded, deterministic preferred-model semantics.
invariants: The method cannot invent a domain fact or lexical relation.
Unrelated updates leave the assessed support relation unchanged.
Contradictory or incomparable preferred extensions return indeterminate rather than an arbitrary binary label.
Control flow is independent of surface vocabulary, source family, row identity, and expected output.
uncertaintySemantics: Compare a declared ordinal support relation over preferred extensions before and after the update; do not interpret binary benchmark labels as probabilities.
proofBehavior: A solved result would cite the compiled propositions, activated defaults, defeated defaults, priority comparisons, and the before/after support relation.
resourceBounds: Finite grounded propositions, finite declared defaults, explicit maximum preferred extensions, and deterministic timeout or budget exhaustion status.
kbMigration: No migration because the proposed input representation and support ordering are not yet specified or implemented.
guardianReasons: Development examples establish several distinct knowledge and semantic-composition gaps, not one executable typed cause.
The existing preferred-entailment method handles explicit finite defaults, but the adapter cannot soundly compile arbitrary source prose into its propositions and priorities.
Adding only the final binary comparison would leave all 14,968 cases without justified symbolic inputs and would not improve benchmark coverage.
A full rename test cannot pass until a typed representation, proof contract, and executable method exist.
